tytul: Pumpkin and apple chutney: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for pumpkin and apple chutney.

ostrzezenia.tekst: NCHFP says that even when vinegar or lemon juice is added, the pH of pumpkin butter varies so much that no single recommendation can be made to ensure a safe product; a large amount of sugar may also not be enough to inhibit pathogens.
According to UGA Extension, pumpkin is a low-acid food, so it needs pressure processing for safe canning, just like vegetables and meats.
The USDA has no tested recipes for safely canning certain pumpkin preserves and storing them at room temperature; for cubed pumpkin, only pressure canning is recommended.

akapity: The FDA list gives pumpkin a pH of about 4.90–5.50.
Pumpkin must not be mashed or puréed for canning.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): pumpkin cooked down in a chutney is treated here like puréed pumpkin, for which home canning is not recommended.

NCHFP has no research data on the proportions and parameters needed to acidify puréed pumpkin products for boiling water canning, and it does not make up or estimate canning processes for low-acid foods.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for pumpkin chutney from a checked source.
